title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with new ventures and partnerships as established players look to expand their influence. Meanwhile, concerns about the health of the ISS and the challenges of hypersonic technology continue to loom large.

themes.title: New Ventures in Megaconstellations
themes.body: Starlink veterans are launching a startup aimed at broadening ownership of megaconstellations, signaling a shift in how satellite networks might be structured. This could lead to increased competition and innovation in the satellite communications market.

themes.title: ISS Health Concerns
themes.body: A recent repair spacewalk at the ISS has brought to light ongoing worries about the station's longevity and operational viability. As the station ages, these issues may necessitate more robust international collaboration to ensure its continued function.

themes.title: Defense Tech and Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting growing recognition of the strategic importance of space in defense. This funding boost may catalyze new projects and partnerships in the defense-tech sector.

themes.title: Hypersonic Technology Delays
themes.body: The latest hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped again, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This trend raises questions about the feasibility and readiness of hypersonic capabilities in the near term.
